title: Shape builders
goal: I can name half circles and quarter circles. I can count shapes and cubes in order. I can use layers to count a stack.

learn.intro: Shapes can be put together and taken apart. A half circle has 1 straight side. A quarter circle has 2 straight sides. To count shapes, work in order and count one kind at a time.

example.problem: Count every square in this grid, big and small. It has 2 rows and 2 columns.
steps: Look for larger squares. One square is 2 by 2: the whole grid. That is 1.

howto.title: How to count shapes
steps: Then count the next size up.

facts.title: Solids
lines: Cylinder: 2 flat circles and 1 curved face.
Cubes in a stack: count layer by layer.

try.text: A grid has 2 rows and 3 columns. How many squares are there, big and small? {b}
try.explanation: Small squares: 2 rows of 3 is 6. Squares 2 by 2: 2 of them. 6 + 2 = 8 squares. There is no 3 by 3 square because the grid is only 2 high.

items.text: Look at the solids. How many flat faces does each solid have?
items.explanation: A cube has 6 flat square faces. A cylinder has 2 flat faces (circles) and 1 curved face. A cone has 1 flat face (a circle) and 1 curved face. A sphere has no flat face: it is all curved.

items.text: Count each kind of piece.
items.explanation: Go through the pieces one kind at a time. Half circles: 3. Quarter circles: 4. Squares: 2. Triangles: 3. Check: 3 + 4 + 2 + 3 = 12 pieces.

items.text: All the circles are the same size.
items.explanation: (a) 2 quarters make a half. (b) Each half is 2 quarters, so 3 halves are 6 quarters. (c) 4 quarters make 1 circle, so 12 quarters make 3 circles.

items.text: Count every square of every size in this grid. Start with the smallest.
items.explanation: 1 by 1 squares: 3 rows of 3 is 9. 2 by 2 squares: they can start in 2 places across and 2 places down, so 4. 3 by 3 square: the whole grid, 1. Total: 9 + 4 + 1 = 14.

items.text: Count the cubes in each stack. Every cube sits on the table or on another cube. Stack A is 1 cube deep. Stacks B and C are 2 cubes deep. At the back they are just like at the front.
items.explanation: A: 3 + 2 + 1 = 6. B has 2 rows, and each row has 2 + 1 = 3 cubes, so 2 × 3 = 6. C has 2 rows of 2 + 2 + 1 = 5 cubes, so 2 × 5 = 10.

items.text: Count the triangles of all sizes. Start with the smallest.
items.explanation: The 2 lines from the top cut the triangle into 3 small triangles. 2 small ones next to each other make a larger triangle: there are 2 such pairs. The whole triangle is 1 more. 3 + 2 + 1 = 6.

items.text: Which solid am I? Circle it.

parts.label: b
parts.text: I have 1 flat circle and 1 curved face.   {circ:cone|cylinder|cube}

parts.label: c
parts.text: I roll and have no flat face.   {circ:sphere|cube|cylinder}

items.explanation: (a) Only a cube has 6 square faces. (b) A cone has one flat circle (its base) and one curved face. (c) A sphere is curved all over. (d) A cylinder has 2 flat circles, one at each end.

items.text: Put the pieces together. Circle the shape you make.
items.explanation: (a) 2 half circles make 1 whole circle. (b) 2 same squares joined side by side make a longer shape with 4 square corners: a rectangle. (c) 4 quarter circles make a whole circle.

items.text: Ali builds a stack of cubes. The bottom layer is 5 cubes long and 2 cubes wide. The stack has 3 layers that are all the same.
items.explanation: (a) A layer is 2 rows of 5: 5 + 5 = 10 cubes. (b) 3 layers of 10 cubes: 10 + 10 + 10 = 30 cubes.

items.text: Name the flat faces.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Each face of a cube is a   {circ:square|circle|triangle}

parts.label: b
parts.text: Each flat face of a cylinder is a   {circ:circle|square|triangle}

parts.label: c
parts.text: The flat face of a cone is a   {circ:triangle|circle|square}

items.explanation: (a) A cube has 6 faces and each one is a square. (b) The 2 flat faces of a cylinder are circles. (c) The flat face of a cone is its base, a circle.

items.text: Beyond: a net folds up into a solid. Which nets fold up into a cube? Every square must become a different face.
items.explanation: A is a cross: a row of 4 squares folds into the 4 sides, one square is the top and one is the bottom. B is a staircase of 3 pairs and folds into a cube. C has a row of 5 squares. The 5th would land on the 1st face, so it does not fold. D has a 2 by 2 block of squares: those 4 squares cannot all be different faces, so it does not fold.
items.hint: A line of 5 squares cannot fold into a cube.

items.text: Count the rectangles in a row of 4 squares. A square is a rectangle too.
items.explanation: 1 square long: 4. 2 squares long: they start at square 1, 2 or 3, so 3. 3 squares long: they start at square 1 or 2, so 2. 4 squares long: 1. Total: 4 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 10.
items.hint: A rectangle 2 squares long can start in 3 places.

items.text: A big triangle has 1 line across. It has 2 lines from its top corner.
items.explanation: The 2 lines from the top and the 2 sloping sides make 4 lines from the top. Choosing 2 of them gives 6 triangles on each line that runs across: 3 small ones, 2 made of 2 parts and 1 made of 3 parts. There are 2 lines across (the base and the middle line): 6 + 6 = 12 triangles.
items.hint: Count the triangles that sit on each line separately.

items.text: Beyond: a pyramid of cubes has 5 layers. The top layer is 1 by 1, then 2 by 2, then 3 by 3, then 4 by 4. The bottom layer is 5 by 5.
Small cubes make a big cube that is 4 long, 4 wide and 4 high. The outside is painted. Count the small cubes with each number of painted faces.
items.explanation: 3 faces: the 8 corners. 2 faces: each of the 12 edges has 2 cubes between the corners, so 24. 1 face: each of the 6 faces has a 2 by 2 middle, so 6 × 4 = 24. No paint: the middle block is 2 by 2 by 2, so 8. Check: 8 + 24 + 24 + 8 = 64 = 4 × 4 × 4.
items.hint: Corners, edges, faces, inside. Check they make 64.

items.text: Design a stack with exactly 24 cubes. Write the cubes in each layer. Many answers are right.

answer.text: Open. Examples: 4 long, 3 wide and 2 high is 12 + 12 = 24. Or layers of 12, 8 and 4 cubes: 12 + 8 + 4 = 24.

items.explanation: Example 1: 4 by 3 by 2: each layer has 12 cubes and there are 2 layers: 24. Example 2: a layer of 4 by 3 (12), a layer of 4 by 2 (8) and a layer of 2 by 2 (4): 12 + 8 + 4 = 24.
items.hint: Each layer needs a layer under it.

items.text: Count the rectangles in a grid with 2 rows and 3 columns. A square counts too. {b}
items.explanation: 1 by 1: 6. 1 high and 2 long: 4. 1 high and 3 long: 2. 2 high and 1 long: 3. 2 high and 2 long: 2. 2 high and 3 long: 1. Total: 6 + 4 + 2 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 18.
items.hint: Sort them by size: 1 by 1, 1 by 2, 1 by 3, 2 by 1, 2 by 2, 2 by 3.

items.text: Which solid has 1 flat face and 1 curved face?   {circ:cube|cone|cylinder}
items.explanation: A cone has a flat circle for its base and one curved face. A cylinder has 2 flat faces.

items.text: All the circles are the same size. 3 half circles make {b} quarter circles.
items.explanation: 1 half circle is 2 quarter circles. 3 half circles make 3 × 2 = 6 quarter circles.

items.text: A stack has 2 layers. Each layer is 4 cubes by 3 cubes. How many cubes? {b}
items.explanation: One layer is 4 × 3 = 12 cubes. There are 2 layers: 12 + 12 = 24.

items.text: A grid has 3 rows and 2 columns. Squares, big and small: {b}
items.explanation: Small squares: 6. Squares 2 by 2: 2. Total: 6 + 2 = 8.
